knowledge:
- key_parameters: DNA=K x S integer count matrix of DNA counts ;; RNA=K x S integer count matrix of RNA counts ;; eid=Character vector of length K identifying the unique putative regulatory elements (PREs) ;; eseq=Optional character vector of length K specifying PRE sequences ;; barcode=Optional character vector of length K specifying barcode sequences ;; aggregate=Method to summarize barcode-level information ("mean" for average estimator, "sum" for aggregate estimator, or "none" if already aggregated) ;; normalize=Logical, if TRUE scales libraries to 10 million reads ;; model_type="indep_groups" for independent samples (unpaired) or "corr_groups" for paired/linked samples ;; block=Integer vector indicating sample/block membership, required when model_type is "corr_groups" ;; endomorphic=Logical, if TRUE returns an MPRASet object with results in rowData and scaled counts in assays instead of an MArrayLM object ;; coef=Coefficient to extract, passed to topTable internally when endomorphic is TRUE
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when performing differential activity analysis of regulatory elements in MPRA data across different conditions (e.g., tissues) or between different alleles (e.g., SNP variants).
- pitfalls: In allelic studies, different alleles are linked to different barcodes and may have varying barcode counts, so counts should be aggregated over barcodes before creating the MPRASet object ;; For paired/allelic analyses, failing to specify the block vector and setting model_type to "corr_groups" will lead to incorrect modeling of within-sample correlation.

workflows.name: tissue_comparison
workflows.intent: Perform differential activity analysis of regulatory elements between independent groups (e.g., tissues or cell types).
workflows.stages: 1. Create an MPRASet object using MPRASet() ;; 2. Define the design matrix ;; 3. Fit the model using mpralm() with model_type = "indep_groups" ;; 4. Extract top differential elements using topTable() ;; 5. Optionally run mpralm() with endomorphic = TRUE to return results directly inside the MPRASet object.
workflows.code:
mpraset_example <- MPRASet(DNA = dna, RNA = rna, eid = eid, eseq = eseq, barcode = NULL)
design <- data.frame(intcpt = 1, episomal = grepl("MT", colnames(mpraSetExample)))
mpralm_fit <- mpralm(object = mpraSetExample, design = design, aggregate = "mean", normalize = TRUE, model_type = "indep_groups", plot = TRUE)
toptab <- topTable(mpralm_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf)
toptab6 <- head(toptab)
efit <- mpralm(object = mpraSetExample, design = design, aggregate = "sum", normalize = TRUE, model_type = "indep_groups", plot = FALSE, endomorphic = TRUE, coef = 2)
rowData(efit)
sdna <- assay(efit, "scaledDNA")
srna <- assay(efit, "scaledRNA")

workflows.name: allelic_comparison
workflows.intent: Perform differential activity analysis between alleles of regulatory elements measured in the same samples (paired analysis).
workflows.stages: 1. Create an MPRASet object using MPRASet() ;; 2. Define the design matrix and block vector ;; 3. Fit the model using mpralm() with model_type = "corr_groups" and specifying the block vector ;; 4. Extract top differential elements using topTable().
workflows.code:
mpraset_example2 <- MPRASet(DNA = agg_dna, RNA = agg_rna, eid = eid, eseq = eseq, barcode = NULL)
design <- data.frame(intcpt = 1, alleleB = grepl("allele_B", colnames(mpraSetAllelicExample)))
block_vector <- rep(1:5, 2)
mpralm_allele_fit <- mpralm(object = mpraSetAllelicExample, design = design, aggregate = "none", normalize = TRUE, block = block_vector, model_type = "corr_groups", plot = TRUE)
toptab_allele <- topTable(mpralm_allele_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf)
head(toptab_allele)
